page: Amazon Web Services r6idn.2xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance powered by a dedicated 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor. Managed under the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores, supported by 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz (an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio). It includes 474 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. The processor incorporates instruction set extensions such as AVX-512, VNNI, AES-NI, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results place the r6idn.2xlarge solidly in the average tier across general compute and memory tasks. Single-core and multi-core evaluations show balanced performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1673.0, a multi-core score of 6164.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 11310.7. Cached memory read throughput reaches 414.14 GB/sec, while large-block uncached read and write bandwidths measure 57.24 GB/sec and 42.33 GB/sec, respectively. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression yields 32.51 GB/sec, which falls into the lower performance quartile.

Workload testing highlights consistent throughput for in-memory and input-output operations. The instance achieves 7.88 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and a static web serving throughput of 12.11 GB/sec. While suitable for lightweight CPU-based language models—delivering 642.28 tokens/sec during prompt processing on a 135M parameter model—it experiences significant latency on 7B models (16.18 tokens/sec prompt processing and 7.46 tokens/sec generation) and lacks hardware acceleration for larger architectures.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bundled 474 GB NVMe SSD and high memory density offer balanced value for workloads requiring fast local scratch disks and ample RAM without adding separate block storage costs. The r6idn.2xlarge is well-suited for medium-scale in-memory databases, caching layers, real-time analytics, and web serving setups requiring local disk caching.
